newsitem.title: USA: CME pork bellies end sharply up on stocks drawdown.
newsitem.headline: CME pork bellies end sharply up on stocks drawdown.

text.p: CME pork belly futures moved up to near limit gains on renewed demand late and finished with sharp advances linked to Tuesday's bullish USDA Cold Storage report and technical buy stops. Hogs also rallied late to close with sharp gains on short covering, traders said.
Pork bellies ended 2.875 to 1.225 cent per lb higher with July up 2.800 at 93.350 cents. Hogs finished up 0.950 to off 0.175 cent with June up most at 81.750 cents.
Pork bellies shrugged off midsession profit taking to run up to new day's highs late as the bullish report and strong technicals combined to rally prices, traders said.

U.S. May 1 frozen pork belly stocks were reported by USDA at 54.017 million lbs, less than 54.767 million on April 1 and under 57.174 million lbs on May 1 of last year. This is only the second time on record that a decline was recorded in stocks during April, analysts said.
Normally, pork bellies are moved into storage in April ahead of the peak U.S. summer demand season.
Technical buy stops were hit at 92.500 cents in the July and again above 93.000, adding to the rise, they said.
"Technically, it looks like they are breaking out to the up side," said Art Paulsrud with ADM Investor Services.
Cargill Investor Services, LFG, R.J. O'Brien and RBH bought bellies late, traders said.
Rand Financials, ING and refco also bought early, pit sources said.
